papers.title_en: Do Large Language Models Play Six Degrees of Separation? Measuring Topological Compression in Long-Context Manifolds
papers.evidence: 通过隐藏状态几何分析解释LLM多跳推理机制
papers.tldr: 大语言模型的多跳推理机制长期依赖注意力分析，但注意力汇聚等伪影掩盖了真实语义距离。本文绕开注意力，直接对长上下文隐藏状态流形进行几何分析：将相似矩阵稀疏化为图，追踪语义锚点连接，发现深层推理层出现尖锐拓扑相变，形成严格受限的小世界网络，任意概念间跳数不超过六度分隔。该几何签名同时用于RAG系统幻觉检测，事实生成保持约3跳结构，幻觉则拓扑坍缩。
papers.abstract_en: Large Language Models (LLMs) demonstrate remarkable multi-hop reasoning capabilities over long contexts, yet the internal mechanisms enabling these distant cognitive leaps remain poorly understood. Traditional attention-based interpretability often fails to capture true semantic proximity due to routing artifacts like attention sinks. In this paper, we bypass attention weights to directly analyze the dynamic geometry of the hidden state manifold, proving that deep LLM latent spaces natively organize into Small-World networks. By sparsifying the continuous similarity matrices of long-context representations into unweighted graphs, we trace the connectivity between highly disjoint semantic anchors across two distinct architectures. Our findings reveal a sharp topological phase transition: while early syntactic layers remain entirely fractured, deep reasoning layers abruptly compress massive conceptual distances into highly navigable pathways strictly bounded by the "Six Degrees of Separation" limit (=< 6 semantic hops). Furthermore, we demonstrate the practical efficacy of this framework by applying it to zero-shot hallucination detection within Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) using the RAGognize dataset. We show that factually grounded generations maintain structural integrity with their source context (approximately 3 hops), whereas hallucinations induce severe topological collapse. Ultimately, this work mathematically formalizes how transformers execute abstract reasoning and provides a novel, strictly geometric signature for evaluating factual reliability.

papers.authors: Michael C. Mozer, Shoaib Ahmed Siddiqui, Danny Sawyer, Sunny Sanyal, Rosanne Liu
papers.evidence: 推理时增强现成基础模型的推理能力
papers.tldr: 传统前馈Transformer的状态更新受限于模型深度，难以有效跟踪信念状态。本文提出循环机制“recirculation”，在不增加生成时延的前提下，通过预填充阶段串行处理增强推理能力。自适应变体仅微调超参数、冻结原模型权重，在Gemma3上使困惑度降低23%、GSM8k准确率提升21%。该方法利用模型自身特性指导架构调整，开辟了无需重训练的架构进化路径。
papers.abstract_en: We describe an inference-time architectural enhancement for off-the-shelf foundation models that markedly reduces perplexity and boosts accuracy across generation and reasoning tasks. Our approach incurs essentially no additional latency during generation, though it requires serial processing in the prefill phase. Motivated by the fundamental limitation that state updates in feedforward transformers are bounded by model depth, our technique, recirculation, introduces a specific form of recurrence that allows the model to act as a dynamical system and track belief states. We distinguish this technique from chain-of-thought computation---which is better reserved for complex inferences rather than basic state tracking---as well as from popular depth-recurrence techniques (looping) and the costly training of recurrent transformers. We also propose and evaluate an adaptive variant of recirculation which requires only light tuning of hyperparameters while freezing the original model weights. Relative to the off-the-shelf baseline, adaptive recirculation achieves remarkable gains on the Gemma3 family, including a 23% reduction in perplexity on a suite of datasets, a 21% increase in accuracy on GSM8k, and reliable improvements in accuracy on other downstream tasks. Our training-free approach succeeds by leveraging the model itself to inform architectural modifications, suggesting a route to architectural evolution guided by a trained network's properties rather than forced, arbitrary design choices.

papers.title_en: Recognition-Conditioned Reasoning: A Training-Free Multimodal-LLM Pipeline for Fine-Grained Micro-Action Understanding
papers.authors: Fengshun Wang, Jin'ang Han, Zhigang Tu
papers.evidence: 无需训练的多模态LLM流水线，对肢体动作进行细粒度识别与推理
papers.tldr: 微动作是细微、短暂、低幅度的身体动作，能泄露情绪与心理状态。现有方法往往只做分类，缺乏对部位运动及类别成因的精细推理。本文提出一种免训练、纯提示词的多模态大语言模型流水线，在禁止微调与真值监督的MA-Bench竞赛中夺冠。系统将八项子任务动态路由至最优的冻结MLLM，判别式模型负责闭集识别，生成式模型负责开放描述与推理。结果显示开放任务平均分2.68，远超第二名1.44，证明了模型路由策略的有效性。
papers.abstract_en: Micro-actions are subtle, short, low-amplitude body movements, such as a fidgeting hand or a slight head tilt, that humans perform with little conscious intent yet that reliably leak emotional and psychological state. Understanding them goes beyond assigning a label: a model must also describe which body parts move and reason, faithfully, about why a clip warrants a particular fine-grained category. We present the training-free, prompt-only system that won first place in the fine-grained understanding track (MA-Bench) of the MAC~2026 Micro-Action Challenge, where both fine-tuning and ground-truth supervision are disallowed. Built entirely upon frozen multimodal large language models (MLLMs), the system dynamically routes each of the eight sub-tasks to the MLLM empirically best suited for that task: a discriminative MLLM for closed-ended recognition tasks and a generative MLLM for open-ended description and reasoning tasks. This architecture achieves a statistically significant performance advantage on open-ended tasks, attaining an average score of 2.68 (on a five-point scale) compared to 1.44 for the second-best approach.
